coverage: Claims were chosen in file order to take every command, flag, setting, path, default and behaviour in the body - the auth.log/secure paths and their on-by-default statement, the process-execution default, the journald/journalctl commands and Storage=persistent setting, the ausearch -k/-ts, ausearch -ui/-ts, aureport --summary, auditctl execve-rule and auditctl -l commands, the auditd rules claims and /etc/audit/rules.d/, every bash-history behaviour and setting (HISTFILE, HISTSIZE, HISTTIMEFORMAT, curl-pipe evasion), every cron/systemd/rc.local/profile/authorized_keys persistence path with crontab -l and systemctl list-unit-files --state=enabled, and the utmp/wtmp/btmp last/lastb/lastlog claims - and each was checked against the only listed source, auditd(8) at man7.org (fetched today, HTTP 200), which documents only the audit daemon's options, signals and file locations.
suggested_edits: The single listed source cannot support this skill: auditd(8) covers only the audit daemon itself, so every command, flag and non-auditd path in the skill is unverifiable. Add per-topic sources and re-check: ausearch(8) and aureport(8) man pages for the -k, -ui, -ts and --summary flags; auditctl(8) or audit.rules(7) for auditctl -l and the 'always,exit -F arch=b64 -S execve' rule syntax; journalctl(1) and journald.conf(5) for -u/--since/--until and Storage=persistent; bash(1) for HISTFILE, HISTSIZE=0, history -c, HISTTIMEFORMAT and write-on-shell-exit semantics; sshd(8) or distro logging docs for /var/log/auth.log vs /var/log/secure and 'Failed password'; cron(8)/crontab(5) for the cron paths and per-user crontab; systemd.unit(5) for /etc/systemd/system vs /lib/systemd/system; last(1)/lastb(1)/lastlog(8) for wtmp/btmp/lastlog. Keep auditd(8) as the source for the /etc/audit/rules.d/ rule-file claim, which it confirms. Also soften 'auditd only logs what explicit rules tell it to' - auditd(8) documents neither that exclusivity nor any rule syntax.
